featured_reviews.name: Joshua Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: Built in 1800 by the North Salsette Society's local Taluka Board, this well was buried under debris and subsequent road developments, lost for years. It was rediscovered in 2018 with the efforts of local water conservationist Vincy Pareira and renovated in 2020 with the support of local corporator Tejasvee Ghosalkar. The mural sculpture depicting the culture and traditions of a typical East Indian village is designed by artists Sachin Waikar and Santosh Waikar.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Trivedi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mandapeshwar Caves in Borivali is a wonderful hidden gem that offers a peaceful break from the city’s hustle. These ancient rock-cut caves, dating back to the 8th century, feature beautiful stone carvings and serve as a serene shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva.
Nestled near Mount Poinsur, the site feels calm and spiritual, making it perfect for devotees, history lovers, or anyone seeking a quiet escape in nature. The intricate sculptures from over 1,200 years ago and timeless beauty create a refreshing atmosphere that leaves you feeling relaxed and inspired. A truly positive and soul soothing visit. Best visited in mornings in summers.

featured_reviews.name: Binay Dangol
featured_reviews.review_text: The Mandapeshwar Caves, located in Borivali, Mumbai, are a significant historical site. These caves, approximately 1.8 km from the Borivali railway station, date back to the 1st century CE. They are renowned for their intricate carvings, including depictions of Lord Vishnu and other deities, highlighting their religious and cultural importance. The site showcases the architectural brilliance of ancient rock-cut temples and offers a glimpse into early Indian religious art and history. You can explore these caves to gain insights into the religious practices and artistry prevalent during that era.

featured_reviews.name: Atharva Malekar

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Mirjolkar
featured_reviews.review_text: Ancient marvel, modern neglect. Mandapeshwar Caves is an incredible piece of Mumbai’s history, but the surroundings are quite disappointing. While the caves and the Shiva Lingam are well-maintained by the priests, the exterior area feels like an abandoned playground. It needs better cleanliness, informative boards, and a dedicated garden/walkway to respect the site's heritage. A must-visit if you can look past the lack of infrastructure.

featured_reviews.name: kirtan raut
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is a historical place having a great significance from the Peshwas regimes. It is believed that there was a secret passage from here to Vasai fort in the reign of Chimajiappa. The pasage was blocked due to untoward incidents happening in them. The scriptures need a renovation to preserve the ruins. In our schools we used to collect oil for lighting lamps here on Tripurari Purnima. Every year the festival was celebrated here and place enlightened with oil lamps was very picturesque. There is Shiva Temple at the center where daily Pooja's are offered by devotees. The garden along the periphery is used as recreational purpose by local who visit the temple and enjoy the recreational space here. The entry to the upper super structure is restricted due to the deterioration of the structure. The structure needs to be revived to it's original Glory.

featured_reviews.name: Questraveler Questraveler
featured_reviews.review_text: This is our ancient treasure. Already British and Portuguese have destroyed many beautiful sculptures of this place but now whatever remains we need to maintain. No cleanliness, not properly maintained. No information written at the place. Only one ASI board is there but history of this place it's importance is not mentioned anywhere. The gabhara is clean (sanctum sanctorum is well maintained) Inside the shivling Pooja is done regularly. Felt blessed in the sanctum sanctorum. On top of the cave remains of old construction are also seen. There is a small garden just outside the caves somehow only that seems to be in good condition. No parking space available. Outside the cave there is riksha stand so very difficult to find a parking place. These caves are located on the main road so easy to reach by auto, bus or own vehicle. Time required to see the place in detail is approximately 30,45 minutes.Do visit when in dahisar. Borivali or near by area.

featured_reviews.name: Sambhaji R Chopdekar
featured_reviews.review_text: After visiting Mandapeshwar caves, we decided to see the Eksar Veergal (hero stones) which is hardly 2 km apart. These beautiful hero stones have been in a private place of a residential building. The gatekeepers of that building are quite helpful, so entering there is not an issue. The place is also being used for feeding stray dogs however the gatekeepers assured us that they are harmless. The hero stones are marvelous, especially the one having the ship used as the battlefield.

featured_reviews.name: Narendra Lakhan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Eksar Herostone
Veeragal’ (Hero Stones)  have intricate carvings and are made of flat basalt. About 8-ft high, the stones were built as a tribute to warriors of the Shilahara dynasty navy.

The stones at Eksar date back to 10-12th century. The uniqueness of these stones is their depiction of Navy Battles.

This important heritage of Mumbai are unique in size and scale and it also a proof that Shilahara dynasty had naval capabilities.

The carved panels depicting ships and sailors  something rarely seen on hero stones, which usually depict land battles.

The Hero stones built up in 12th Centrury Shilahara dynasty and had a navy and fought a sea battle.

featured_reviews.name: Ramprasad Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text: Simply brilliant and historic. The quality, composition and finish achieved in this "veergal" creation and execution is straightforward top-of-the-line professional. All the schools and colleges must take their children for such an excursion. On the top one can see Ghata Palav, a pot with dead man ashes as if the hero as an hero's welcome in the heaven with luscious damsels accompanying the hero. Herostones indeed! At Borivli west. Google Eksar stone.

A Complete Scam. Total Waste of Money!
​Rating: ⭐☆☆☆☆
​If you are thinking about using Swayourway, do yourself a huge favor and close the tab right now. This company is a masterclass in how to alienate customers.
​Glitchy & Broken Platform: The entire service is completely unstable. Features that are heavily advertised either don't work at all or constantly crash mid-task. I spent hours trying to get things running smoothly, only to lose all my progress due to their buggy interface.
​Zero Accountability (Ghosted!): When the platform inevitably failed, I reached out for urgent technical support. Days went by without a single reply. They completely ghosted me after taking my payment. There is absolutely no post-purchase support.
​Impossible Refund Policy: When I realized the service was completely unusable, I requested a refund under their supposed "satisfaction guarantee." Of course, they pulled out obscure, hidden clauses from their terms and conditions to deny it.

​They are quick to charge your card, but non-existent when you actually need the service to work. It feels less like a legitimate business and more like a cash-grab. Avoid them like the plague!

featured_reviews.name: Noel Nadar
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is indeed beautiful! It definitely exceeded my expectations. It's the perfect place to sit and relax for hours. The greenery is so peaceful. The view is amazing from the top. All these years I've been in Mumbai, but I didn't know about this amazing hidden location in Dahisar. We visited this place on a weekend by taking the 462 AC bus from Borivali station the East side exit. The climb from here is through a small village here. Vaghdevi Waterfall was a great trek and a good place to enjoy waterfalls during monsoons. You could visit this place with your friends. There's also another exit towards Mira Road side, if you take the longer walking route. One negative aspect is that some people come here and indulge in consuming alcohol and throw the bottles there on the path which is dangerous for people and with the other people throwing plastic waste here it's just destroying the flora and fauna. It's a highly recommended place if you're looking for an adventurous weekend with your friends. This place is a gem in monsoons, enjoying the waterfall and nature in the rains with amazing scenic views. The view from the top is totally worth the climb.

featured_reviews.name: Remon
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vaghdevi waterfalls is a medium level trekking spot great for people who are looking for a short adventure in all the hustle and bustle.

Info:
It takes approximately 3 hrs to go to the top and come back assuming you are spending 10-20 mins at the top.

Best time to visit:
-During mild rains or when it is cold during morning time.
-8-9am is the sweet spot to start you're trekk

Note:
-There are tricky spots to get through but nothing too difficult. Consider this when you are taking a huge group as everyone will not be able to make it through.
-The trekk will definitely be exhausting for first timers.
-Try to reach at top with only one break as muscles will tighten if you take more breaks and it will be tough to complete then.
-Urge you guys not to leave trekk half way as reaching at the top is worth it.
-Take only sips of water and don't drink a lot while climbing.

Things to carry:
-Some eatables(Protein bars chips etc)
- 2 bottles of water per person.

Attire:
-Shoes (Compulsorily)
-Tracks or shorts
-T shirt

PLEASE DONT THROW WASTE AROUND. KEEP IT IN YOU'RE BAG AND THROUGH IT LATER.
HUMBLE REQUEST

My ratings:
Difficult 3/5
Ambiance 4/5
Worth it 5/5
Overall satisfaction 5/5

featured_reviews.name: Bhoomika Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my 2nd trip with Just2Wander
We went to Karjat for camping and I must say one of best camp I've ever been to.......the location was very pretty, the property is very spacious and big that it will take entire day to explore.....
The food, ambience, lots of activities both indoor and outdoor, dancing, live music, zumba, kayaking, pottery, and there was also free night trek which was available...if anyone wants to go for camping this shall be on your list☺️☺️
Had lot's of fun thankyou for this amazing experience 🫶🏼🫶🏼

featured_reviews.name: Apeksha Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
